lotr.waypoint.HIMLING.info: The peak of the hill of Himring, mostly drowned following the War of Wrath.
lotr.waypoint.TOL_FUIN.info: The highlands of Taur-nu-Fuin, the Forest under Nightshade, which survived the drowning of Beleriand.
lotr.waypoint.TOL_MORWEN.info: A lone hill spared in the drowning of Beleriand, upon which lay the grave of Morwen mother of Túrin Turambar.
lotr.waypoint.MENELTARMA_SUMMIT.info: The summit of the Meneltarma, the Sacred Mountain, which alone survived the downfall of Númenor.
lotr.waypoint.HOBBITON.info: A town of Hobbits in the centre of the Shire, overlooked by the Hill of Bag End.
lotr.waypoint.BRANDYWINE_BRIDGE.info: A bridge across the River Brandywine and out of the Shire.
lotr.waypoint.SARN_FORD.info: A stone ford on the southern edge of the Shire. Though the Shire-folk do not know, it is carefully guarded.
lotr.waypoint.LONGBOTTOM.info: A town in the Southfarthing of the Shire, famous for its Longbottom Leaf.
lotr.waypoint.MICHEL_DELVING.info: The chief town of the Shire, located in the White Downs, and home to the Mayor of Michel Delving.
lotr.waypoint.WILLOWBOTTOM.info: A small village near the Woody End.
lotr.waypoint.BUCKLEBURY.info: The chief village of Buckland, home of the Master of Buckland.
lotr.waypoint.WHITFURROWS.info: A small town upon the East Road.
lotr.waypoint.FROGMORTON.info: A village upon the East Road by the Frog-marshes.
lotr.waypoint.OATBARTON.info: A village in the Northfarthing of the Shire.
lotr.waypoint.SCARY.info: A small Hobbit village among caves and stony hills.
lotr.waypoint.NEEDLEHOLE.info: A town in the Westfarthing of the Shire.
lotr.waypoint.LITTLE_DELVING.info: A smaller Hobbit town upon the White Downs.
lotr.waypoint.WAYMEET.info: A town upon the crossing of important Shire-roads.
lotr.waypoint.TUCKBOROUGH.info: A historic town within the Green Hill Country. Home to the Took family, the Thains of the Shire.
lotr.waypoint.NOBOTTLE.info: A town in the Westfarthing of the Shire.
lotr.waypoint.TIGHFIELD.info: A village known for its rope-makers.
lotr.waypoint.BROCKENBORINGS.info: A warren of tunnels within the rocky hills surrounding Scary.
lotr.waypoint.DEEPHALLOW.info: A village upon the banks of the River Brandywine.
lotr.waypoint.STOCK.info: A town upon the Stock-brook by the banks of the River Brandywine.
lotr.waypoint.BYWATER.info: A village by the Pool upon the Water, home of the famous Green Dragon inn.
lotr.waypoint.OVERHILL.info: A small village north of Hobbiton and the Hill.
lotr.waypoint.HAYSEND.info: A village in the south of Buckland at the end of the Hedge.
lotr.waypoint.HAY_GATE.info: The guarded North Gate in the Hedge of Buckland.
lotr.waypoint.GREENHOLM.info: A small town upon the Far Downs at the western border of the Shire.
lotr.waypoint.WITHYWINDLE_VALLEY.info: A strange and haunted valley where the Withywindle runs through the Old Forest.
lotr.waypoint.FORLOND.info: A harbour-city of the Elves on the northern shore of the Gulf of Lune.
lotr.waypoint.HARLOND.info: A harbour-city of the Elves on the southern shore of the Gulf of Lune.
lotr.waypoint.MITHLOND_NORTH.info: The northern half of Mithlond, the Grey Havens, where Círdan the Shipwright dwells with his people.
lotr.waypoint.MITHLOND_SOUTH.info: The southern half of Mithlond, the Grey Havens, where Círdan the Shipwright dwells with his people.
lotr.waypoint.FORLINDON.info: The northern regions of the fair country of Lindon.
lotr.waypoint.HARLINDON.info: The southern regions of the fair country of Lindon.
lotr.waypoint.TOWER_HILLS.info: Tallest of the White Towers built for Elendil by Gil-galad, said to house one of the Seeing Stones of Arnor.
lotr.waypoint.AMON_EREB.info: An ancient hill in Lindon, which, long ago in the Elder Days, was a lookout-post of great importance.
lotr.waypoint.BELEGOST.info: An ancient Dwarven city of the Blue Mountains, dating back to the Elder Days. It was destroyed after the War of Wrath, but later resettled, in part.
lotr.waypoint.NOGROD.info: An ancient Dwarven city of the Blue Mountains, dating back to the Elder Days. It was destroyed after the War of Wrath, but later resettled, in part.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_RERIR.info: A large mountain ruined long ago during the War of Wrath. In Elder Days a fortress of Caranthir son of Fëanor stood upon its slopes.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_DOLMED.info: Said to be the awakening-place of two Fathers of the Dwarves, this mountain was cloven in the War of Wrath and diminished in size.
lotr.waypoint.THORIN_HALLS.info: Once ruled by Thorin Oakenshield, this settlement in the Blue Mountains is inhabited by Dwarves mostly of Durin's Folk.
lotr.waypoint.ARVEDUI_MINES.info: Abandoned mines in the Blue Mountains. The last King of Arnor and his company once hid here to escape the threat of Angmar.
lotr.waypoint.THRAIN_HALLS.info: A Dwarven settlement, founded by Thráin and the exiles of the Lonely Mountain, with many old mines still in use today.
lotr.waypoint.NORTH_DOWNS.info: A range of hills in northern Eriador with the ancient city of Fornost Erain at their southwestern end.
lotr.waypoint.SOUTH_DOWNS.info: A range of hills in Eriador.
lotr.waypoint.ERYN_VORN.info: These dark woodlands are among the last remnants of the ancient forest that once covered all Eriador.
lotr.waypoint.THARBAD.info: An old ford-town in Eriador, deserted following the Great Plague.
lotr.waypoint.FORNOST.info: Fornost Erain, the ruined capital of Arnor. Known as Kings' Norbury in the Common Tongue.
lotr.waypoint.ANNUMINAS.info: The old capital of Arnor, the North-kingdom, before it was abandoned in favour of Fornost Erain.
lotr.waypoint.GREENWAY_CROSSROADS.info: The crossing of the great East-West and North-South roads.
lotr.waypoint.BREE.info: The chief town of the Bree-land, known for its cheerful Men and Hobbits.
lotr.waypoint.STADDLE.info: A town of Hobbits in the Bree-land.
lotr.waypoint.COMBE.info: A village of Men on the road to the Chetwood.
lotr.waypoint.ARCHET.info: A town of the Bree-folk on the edge of the Chetwood with a lively logging trade.
lotr.waypoint.FORSAKEN_INN.info: A day's ride east of Bree, this lonely inn is the last settlement of Men before the wild lands.
lotr.waypoint.WEATHERTOP.info: The ruined watchtower of Amon Sûl. In olden days it housed one of the great Seeing Stones of Arnor.
lotr.waypoint.LAST_BRIDGE.info: The last bridge on the Great East Road before the Misty Mountains.
lotr.waypoint.OLD_ELF_WAY.info: An old road once travelled by Elves of Eregion.
lotr.waypoint.RIVENDELL.info: The hidden valley of Imladris, where Lord Elrond dwells with his people in the Last Homely House East of the Sea.
lotr.waypoint.FORD_BRUINEN.info: The shallow ford crossing the Loudwater into the realm of Rivendell.
lotr.waypoint.THE_TROLLSHAWS.info: A wild and outlandish forest, scattered with old castles and ruins of Rhudaur, and dark caves home to Trolls from the mountains.
lotr.waypoint.CARN_DUM.info: The capital of the old Kingdom of Angmar.
lotr.waypoint.WEST_GATE.info: The western gate of Khazad-dûm, now called Moria: of old the great delvings and mansions of the Dwarves of Durin's Folk and a wonder of the Northern world.
lotr.waypoint.OST_IN_EDHIL.info: The ruined city of the Elves of Eregion.
lotr.waypoint.NORTH_DUNLAND.info: A village of shepherds and hunters in the northern reaches of Dunland.
lotr.waypoint.SOUTH_DUNLAND.info: A town of middling size in the highs of Dunland, and a stop for many traders and travellers on their journeys through the region.
lotr.waypoint.FORDS_OF_ISEN.info: These shallow fords across the River Isen into Rohan are often the site of skirmishes between the Rohirrim and the Orcs.
lotr.waypoint.DWARROWVALE.info: A Dunlending village grown up around the site of an old hamlet, which, it is said, once hosted Thráin and Thorin Oakenshield during their long wanderings in the wild.
lotr.waypoint.WULFBURG.info: Once the fortress of Freca's son, the self-styled 'King' Wulf, who seized Meduseld for Dunland during the reign of Helm Hammerhand.
lotr.waypoint.LOND_DAER.info: The ancient ruins of the first Númenórean haven in Middle-earth.
lotr.waypoint.ENEDWAITH_ROAD.info: With the North-kingdom long fallen and the power of the South-kingdom waning, these stretches of the old Royal Road have long since fallen into ruin.
lotr.waypoint.MOUTHS_ISEN.info: Here the River Isen flows into the Sea after its long course through sparsely-inhabited Enedwaith.
lotr.waypoint.ISENGARD.info: A great fortified ring of stone within a vale of the Misty Mountains, wherein stands the tower of Orthanc, stronghold of Saruman.
lotr.waypoint.CAPE_OF_FOROCHEL.info: The perilous floes of the Icebay, where only the Snowmen of Forochel dare wander.
lotr.waypoint.SOUTH_FOROCHEL.info: One of few permanent settlements of the Lossoth among the frozen wastes.
lotr.waypoint.WITHERED_HEATH.info: A scorched valley in the Grey Mountains where, it is said, lurk the last of the Fire-drakes.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_GUNDABAD.info: The mountain beneath which Durin the Deathless awoke in the Elder Days, and a sacred site of the Dwarves before being overrun by Orcs.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_GRAM.info: A mountain inhabited by Orcs who often trouble the lands of Eriador.
lotr.waypoint.HIGH_PASS.info: A long and perilous mountain pass from Eriador into Wilderland.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_CARADHRAS.info: The Redhorn, one of three peaks above the delvings of Khazad-dûm. The mountain is called Caradhras the Cruel and is said to have a will of its own.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_CELEBDIL.info: The Silvertine, one of the peaks above Khazad-dûm. Upon its summit stands the fabled Durin's Tower.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_FANUIDHOL.info: The Cloudyhead, one of three peaks above the realm of Khazad-dûm.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_METHEDRAS.info: The Last Peak, southermost of the Misty Mountains, whence flow the Rivers Isen and Entwash.
lotr.waypoint.GOBLIN_TOWN.info: A warren of weaving tunnels and caverns beneath the High Pass, where Orcs scutter and scrape in the dark.
lotr.waypoint.EAGLES_EYRIE.info: A great shelf of rock on the eastern side of the Misty Mountains that can be reached only by flight. The Eagles of Manwë reside here.
lotr.waypoint.DAINS_HALLS.info: A colony of Durin's Folk in the Grey Mountains, abandoned after Dáin was slain by a Cold-drake.
lotr.waypoint.SCATHA.info: Once the lair of Scatha, a great Long-worm, before he was slain by Fram of the Éothéod.
lotr.waypoint.CARROCK.info: A towering pillar of rock in the midst of the Great River. It was once said that, on clear nights, a great bear could be seen climbing the rock to gaze upon the Moon.
lotr.waypoint.OLD_FORD.info: The crossing of the Old Forest Road upon the Great River of Wilderland. A bridge once stood here, but has long since crumbled.
lotr.waypoint.GLADDEN_FIELDS.info: The watery meeting-place where the Gladden flows down into the Great River Anduin.
lotr.waypoint.DIMRILL_DALE.info: Azanulbizar, below the East Gate of Khazad-dûm: the valley of the Mirrormere, wherein it is said Durin the Deathless first saw his crown among the stars.
lotr.waypoint.FIELD_OF_CELEBRANT.info: The site of the Gondor-Éothéod victory over the Balchoth, which led to the historic Oath of Cirion and Eorl.
lotr.waypoint.RAUROS.info: The shores of Parth Galen by the great falls of Rauros.
lotr.waypoint.BEORN.info: A rustic homestead inhabited by skin-changers and men of the Vales, said to be unfriendly to outsiders.
lotr.waypoint.FOREST_GATE.info: Once the entrance to the Wood-elven realm in Greenwood the Great, the gate of Mirkwood is now defiled by servants of the Enemy.
lotr.waypoint.FRAMSBURG.info: The ruined city of the Éothéod, Northmen ancestors of the Rohirrim.
lotr.waypoint.ANDUIN_CROSSROADS.info: A fork in the path between the Anduin Road and the road to Dol Guldur.
lotr.waypoint.EAST_RHOVANION_ROAD.info: An old crossroads at the meeting of the Anduin Vales, the Brown Lands, and eastern Wilderland.
lotr.waypoint.THRANDUIL_HALLS.info: The underground halls of Thranduil the Elvenking. It is said that they recall the glory of Menegroth in days of old.
lotr.waypoint.DOL_GULDUR.info: The Hill of Sorcery: fortress-lair of the Necromancer before he fled eastwards, now inhabited by Khamûl the Easterling and his fell servants.
lotr.waypoint.MIRKWOOD_MOUNTAINS.info: The Emyn-nu-Fuin, a range of dark hills rising out of the fog of Mirkwood, which fence out the worst of the Necromancer's corruption.
lotr.waypoint.RHOSGOBEL.info: The dwelling-place of Radagast the Brown, home to many birds and beasts, and a safe haven among the corruption of Mirkwood.
lotr.waypoint.ENCHANTED_RIVER.info: Here the Elf-path crosses over a gloomy black river. It is advised to avoid these waters, for whoever touches them shall not awake...
lotr.waypoint.RIVER_GATE.info: An outpost of the Wood-elves at the end of the Old Forest Road, where it meets the River Running.
lotr.waypoint.EAST_BIGHT.info: Once a thriving region of the Greenwood, the axes of Men have reduced it to a field of stumps and broken trees.
lotr.waypoint.OLD_RHOVANION.info: Long ago, these lands were held by a great Mannish kingdom of Rhovanion, but now its ruins are all that remain.
lotr.waypoint.DORWINION_CROSSROADS.info: A crossing in the great roads of Dale and Dorwinion.
lotr.waypoint.EREBOR.info: The Lonely Mountain. Herein lies the Kingdom under the Mountain, a realm of Durin's Folk.
lotr.waypoint.DALE_CITY.info: The prosperous city of the Kingdom of Dale at the foot of the Lonely Mountain. It was destroyed by Smaug the Terrible in days of old, but rebuilt under King Bard.
lotr.waypoint.LONG_LAKE.info: Upon the Long Lake stands Lake-town, a Northman settlement bustling with trade. Great wealth flows through this town out of Dale and onward to southern lands.
lotr.waypoint.RUNNING_FORD.info: A shallow ford on the River Running where the road runs south to old Rhovanion.
lotr.waypoint.REDWATER_FORD.info: A ford on the Redwater at the eastern border of the Kingdom of Dale, upon the ancient East-West Road laid by the Dwarves.
lotr.waypoint.DALE_CROSSROADS.info: At the meeting of several important Dalish roads, the lands around this crossing are home to many guilds and thriving markets.
lotr.waypoint.DALE_PORT.info: The southern port of the Kingdom of Dale, and an important point on the trade routes of Dorwinion.
lotr.waypoint.WEST_PEAK.info: The nearer of two large peaks in the Iron Hills. Beneath are the halls of Dáin Ironfoot.
lotr.waypoint.EAST_PEAK.info: A large mountain at the far eastern end of the Iron Hills.
lotr.waypoint.CARAS_GALADHON.info: The city of the Galadhrim in Lothlórien, and the heart of Elvendom on earth.
lotr.waypoint.CERIN_AMROTH.info: A great green hill in the midst of Lothlórien from where it is said one may see as far as southern Mirkwood.
lotr.waypoint.NIMRODEL.info: The former home of an Elf-maiden, Nimrodel, who disappeared grieving after her beloved Amroth was drowned in the Sundering Seas.
lotr.waypoint.DERNDINGLE.info: A meeting-place for the Ents of Fangorn, set within a hidden clearing.
lotr.waypoint.WELLINGHALL.info: One of Treebeard's Ent-houses nestled among the spurs of Mount Methedras.
lotr.waypoint.TREEBEARD_HILL.info: A rocky shelf, standing above the trees of Fangorn Forest, where one can contemplate the sunlight on the leaves and the wind among their branches.
lotr.waypoint.WOLD.info: A small town in the sparsely inhabited uplands of Rohan.
lotr.waypoint.EDORAS.info: The chief city of the Riddermark, built upon a hill crowned with the Golden Hall of Meduseld.
lotr.waypoint.HELMS_DEEP.info: The great Rohirric fortress of the Hornburg, which stands in a wide vale beneath the Thrihyrne. Men say that its Deeping Wall has never to this day been breached.
lotr.waypoint.HELMS_CROSSROADS.info: The vale at the foot of Helm's Deep.
lotr.waypoint.URUK_HIGHLANDS.info: These lands in the foothills of the Mountains once belonged to Rohan, but are now desolate and burnt by the servants of the White Hand.
lotr.waypoint.MERING_STREAM.info: This stream marks the border between Rohan and Gondor. It runs through Firienholt, the Whispering Wood.
lotr.waypoint.ENTWADE.info: A ford across the river Entwash, bridging the Eastemnet and the Westemnet.
lotr.waypoint.EASTMARK.info: The heart of the wide lands patrolled by the eastern Riders of Rohan.
lotr.waypoint.ALDBURG.info: The first capital of Rohan, Aldburg is the oldest town in the Riddermark and the seat of the Third Marshal of the Rohirrim.
lotr.waypoint.GRIMSLADE.info: The home of Grimbold, a Marshal of the Riddermark.
lotr.waypoint.CORSAIRS_LANDING.info: In the days of Helm Hammerhand, a fleet of Southrons landed here and fought alongside the Dunlendings to defeat the Men of Rohan.
lotr.waypoint.FRECA_HOLD.info: The old fort raised by the heedless Lord Freca, who ruled the lands around the River Adorn, and was said to be part-Dunlending.
lotr.waypoint.DUNHARROW.info: A refuge of the Rohirrim beneath the Dwimorberg, the Haunted Mountain. It is said that none living may pass the Paths of the Dead.
lotr.waypoint.TARLANG.info: Men say that a giant fell here and broke his neck, forming the mountain pass between the Blackroot Vale and Lamedon.
lotr.waypoint.RAS_MORTHIL.info: The last peak at the headland of the western White Mountains. The Men of Anfalas say that wild Púkel-men still linger in these lands.
lotr.waypoint.MINAS_TIRITH.info: The great Tower of Guard, capital city of the kingdom of Gondor, built of seven levels of pure white stone with the bright Tower of Ecthelion at its summit.
lotr.waypoint.CAIR_ANDROS.info: A fortified island in the Anduin, named for the white foam of the waters that run beside it.
lotr.waypoint.HALIFIRIEN.info: The Holy Mountain, westernmost of the beacon-hills of Gondor. Elendil was once entombed here, and Cirion and Eorl swore their Oath upon its slopes.
lotr.waypoint.CALENHAD.info: The sixth beacon-hill, lit only in times of urgency.
lotr.waypoint.MINRIMMON.info: The fifth beacon-hill and one of the oldest, established before the founding of Rohan.
lotr.waypoint.ERELAS.info: The fourth beacon-hill of Gondor. Bare and treeless, it is easily sighted from the surrounding lands.
lotr.waypoint.NARDOL.info: The third beacon-hill, built on a stretch of the White Mountains. On a clear night its fire is said to be seen all the way from the Halifirien.
lotr.waypoint.EILENACH.info: The second beacon-hill from Minas Tirith, and the highest point of the Drúadan Forest.
lotr.waypoint.AMON_DIN.info: The Silent Hill is the closest beacon to Minas Tirith. Overlooking northern Ithilien, it serves as a fortified outpost for the White City.
lotr.waypoint.OSGILIATH_WEST.info: The crumbling western half of Gondor’s former capital city. Garrisons are housed here to hold the Anduin under Gondorian control.
lotr.waypoint.OSGILIATH_EAST.info: The ruined eastern half of Gondor’s former capital city, now often the site of clashes between Gondorians and Orcs.
lotr.waypoint.EMYN_ARNEN.info: In better days these hills were the residence of some noble and wealthy Gondorian families, including the House of the Stewards.
lotr.waypoint.HENNETH_ANNUN.info: The Forbidden Pool of Ithilien, where the Window-curtain waterfall masks a secret refuge.
lotr.waypoint.CROSSROADS_ITHILIEN.info: These neglected crossroads once housed a majestic statue of a King, which, though now ruined, still wears a coronal of silver and gold.
lotr.waypoint.NORTH_ITHILIEN.info: The northern reaches of the Land of the Moon.
lotr.waypoint.CROSSINGS_OF_POROS.info: The crossing into Harondor over the River Poros. Nearby stands a great mound, wherein rest the twin sons of King Folcwine of Rohan.
lotr.waypoint.PELARGIR.info: The great royal havens of the Ship-kings: the chief harbour of Gondor.
lotr.waypoint.LINHIR.info: A river-town in southern Gondor upon the road from Pelargir to Ethring.
lotr.waypoint.ANDUIN_MOUTH.info: The Mouths of Anduin, home to poor fisher-folk of Gondor.
lotr.waypoint.IMLOTH_MELUI.info: The sweet Valley of Roses within Lossarnach.
lotr.waypoint.CROSSINGS_ERUI.info: The fords of the River Erui in Lossarnach. Many Gondorians once perished here in the Kin-strife.
lotr.waypoint.CALEMBEL.info: A town in Lamedon near the fords of the River Ciril, with few inhabitants.
lotr.waypoint.ETHRING.info: A long bridge in the Ringló Vale on the road from Pelargir to Erech.
lotr.waypoint.ERECH.info: A great steep hill, believed to be haunted, and known for the mysterious black stone which stands upon the summit.
lotr.waypoint.GREEN_HILLS.info: The beautiful Green Hills of Gondor.
lotr.waypoint.DOL_AMROTH.info: A mighty castle and city upon the shores of Belfalas, ruled by the Prince of Dol Amroth, a subject of Gondor.
lotr.waypoint.EDHELLOND.info: An ancient harbour of the Sindar in southern Gondor. The Elves who once dwelt at these havens sailed West long ago.
lotr.waypoint.TARNOST.info: A city in Gondor built in ancient days by Elves who have long since sailed West.
lotr.waypoint.TOLFALAS_ISLAND.info: A bleak abandoned isle in the Bay of Belfalas.
lotr.waypoint.AMON_HEN.info: The Hill of Sight, an ancient seat of Gondorian power.
lotr.waypoint.AMON_LHAW.info: The Hill of Hearing, an ancient seat of Gondorian power.
lotr.waypoint.ARGONATH.info: The Pillars of the Kings: two mighty statues of Isildur and Anárion beside the Anduin, which guard what was once the northern border of Gondor.
lotr.waypoint.NORTH_UNDEEP.info: The northern of two westward bends in the Great River Anduin. The shallow fords of the Undeeps were often used by armies as a crossing-point.
lotr.waypoint.SOUTH_UNDEEP.info: The southern of two westward bends in the Great River Anduin. The shallow fords of the Undeeps were often used by armies as a crossing-point.
lotr.waypoint.MORANNON.info: The great gates of Mordor, wrought of twisted steel and dark stone. None pass unless the Eye of the Dark Tower wills it.
lotr.waypoint.UDUN.info: The Orc-infested vale behind the Black Gates. Named in imitation of Udûn, the first fortress of Morgoth, also called Utumno.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_DOOM.info: Orodruin, the great Fire-mountain in the heart of Mordor, wherein Sauron forged the One Ring long ago.
lotr.waypoint.BARAD_DUR.info: The Dark Tower: fortress of Sauron, Lord of the Earth, and the seat from which all the evil hosts of Mordor are bent to his will.
lotr.waypoint.MINAS_MORGUL.info: Once Minas Ithil, the fair Tower of the Moon; now a dark and sickly place ruled by the Lord of the Nazgûl.
lotr.waypoint.DURTHANG.info: A powerful Orcish stronghold built upon the slopes of Ephel Dúath.
lotr.waypoint.CARACH_ANGREN.info: The Iron Teeth, a guarded mountain pass between Udûn and the plateau of Gorgoroth.
lotr.waypoint.CIRITH_UNGOL.info: The dark and twisted Spider's Cleft within the mountains of Mordor, watched over by an evil guard-tower.
lotr.waypoint.MORIGOST.info: A watch-post upon the shadowy spurs of the Ephel Dúath.
lotr.waypoint.NARGROTH.info: The Halls of Fire, a watchtower above the pass into the plateau of Gorgoroth.
lotr.waypoint.AMON_ANGREN.info: A dark hill in Mordor, upon which stands a fortress of the Nazgûl.
lotr.waypoint.SEREGOST.info: A fortress in the Mountains of Mordor. The armies of the Easterlings pass through here on the road to Barad-dûr.
lotr.waypoint.FELLBEASTS.info: A dark valley behind the walls of Mordor infested with fell beasts and evil creatures.
lotr.waypoint.EASTERN_GUARD.info: A fortress that keeps watch over the road into Mordor out of Rhûn.
lotr.waypoint.NURNEN_NORTHERN_SHORE.info: The dreary northern shores of the Sea of Núrnen.
lotr.waypoint.NURNEN_SOUTHERN_SHORE.info: The bleak southern shores of the Sea of Núrnen.
lotr.waypoint.NURNEN_WESTERN_SHORE.info: The sad western shores of the Sea of Núrnen.
lotr.waypoint.NURNEN_EASTERN_SHORE.info: The dim eastern shores of the Sea of Núrnen.
lotr.waypoint.THAURBAND.info: A terrible prison-fortress of Mordor upon the shores of Núrnen.
lotr.waypoint.VALLEY_OF_SPIDERS.info: A grim and shadowy corner of Mordor, infested with the spawn of Ungoliant.
lotr.waypoint.DORWINION_PORT.info: The Wine-havens upon the Celduin, where the Avarin Elves of Dorwinion receive shipments from their kin in the Woodland Realm.
lotr.waypoint.DORWINION_COURT.info: The shining centre of all trade, learning, and culture within the Mannish realm of Dorwinion.
lotr.waypoint.DORWINION_FORD.info: A crossing out of Dorwinion into the lands of Rhúdel.
lotr.waypoint.DORWINION_HILLS.info: A high peak in the hills of Dorwinion.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_ROAD_WAY.info: A far stretch of the ancient Dwarf-road that runs eastward to the great halls and mansions of the Orocarni.
lotr.waypoint.BALCARAS.info: A city of the Wainriders and one of their few permanent dwelling-places in the wide lands of the East.
lotr.waypoint.KHAND_NORTH_ROAD.info: Here the great tributary road of Sauron runs out of Khand and into the wide lands of Rhûn.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_CAPITAL.info: The greatest city of Rhûn, palace and fortress of the King of the East. Its high towers are wreathed in mist and its mighty gates are inlaid with gold.
lotr.waypoint.KHAMUL_TOWER.info: The sorcerous tower of Khamûl, a cruel king of Easterlings in the Second Age.
lotr.waypoint.MORDOR_FORD.info: The waters of this ford run grey with foul ash. Here, Easterlings may follow the road down into Mordor, or take the long march West.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_NORTH_CITY.info: The bustling markets and twisting streets of this Easterling seaport city are said to confuse travellers from all lands.
lotr.waypoint.BAZYLAN.info: A city of the Easterlings, said to be founded by a mighty nobleman of legend and named for his beloved cat.
lotr.waypoint.BORDER_TOWN.info: A town by the borders of Rhúdel that has grown rich from trade with Dorwinion.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_SEA_CITY.info: A town close to the heart of Rhúdel. It is said that here, on the clearest days, one can glimpse the Isle in the Sea among the far mists.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_NORTH_FORD.info: A ford across the River Forunen on the ancient East-West Road.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_NORTHEAST.info: The northern frontier of Rhúdel, a place of deep bogs and tall brown reeds thick with the terrible air of decay.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_SOUTH_PASS.info: It is said that this mountain pass was once the lair of a great Were-worm out of the South, until Lord Sauron cast the beast into long sleep with a mighty spell.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_EAST_CITY.info: An eastern city of Rhúdel beyond the hills. Trade passes from here down through the wide lands of Rhûn and into the Gulf of Harad.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_EAST_TOWN.info: A small fortified town on the east road to the city of Karslan.
lotr.waypoint.RHUN_SOUTHEAST.info: The southern frontier of Rhúdel, where the road runs on to Sauron's servants in Khand and the Harad.
lotr.waypoint.BARAZ_DUM.info: The Red Delvings: mansions of the Eastern Dwarves beneath the peaks of the Orocarni.
lotr.waypoint.CROSSINGS_OF_HARAD.info: This river marks the border of the contested land of Harondor. From here, the road runs on southwards into the vast Sunlands of the Haradwaith.
lotr.waypoint.HARNEN_SEA_TOWN.info: Where the mighty Harnen river meets the Bay of Belfalas stands the greatest stronghold of the Harnedhrim, a rallying-point against their foes to the North.
lotr.waypoint.HARNEN_ROAD_TOWN.info: A Southron town beyond the crossings of the Harnen, built upon the meeting of many roads.
lotr.waypoint.HARNEN_BLACK_TOWN.info: A small but fortified town of Harnennor. The Haradrim speak of a time when Lord Sauron sent a rain of ash upon their lands, to deliver them from Gondorian invaders.
lotr.waypoint.CROSSINGS_OF_LITHNEN.info: The fords over the river Lithnen and on to eastern lands. Often in ages past were these waters stained red by the conquering swords of Gondor.
lotr.waypoint.HARNEN_RIVER_TOWN.info: A settlement of the Southrons by the river Harnen. Here stands a gruesome tower decorated with the skulls of fallen Northerlings.
lotr.waypoint.KHAND_FORD.info: A crossing into the realm of Khand, which separates Harad from Rhûn.
lotr.waypoint.UMBAR_CITY.info: The proud city of the Black Númenóreans and the Corsairs, nearest of the great realms of Harad, with a long and brutal history of strife against Gondor.
lotr.waypoint.UMBAR_GATE.info: The low pass into the fief-lands of Umbar.
lotr.waypoint.GATE_HERUMOR.info: A great fortress, said to have been constructed long ago on the orders of Herumor himself, which has stood guard over the Bay of Umbar ever since.
lotr.waypoint.CEDAR_ROAD.info: The wood of the cedar tree is valued highly by the Southrons. As Sauron rises in Mordor, he demands incredible amounts as tribute.
lotr.waypoint.FERTILE_VALLEY.info: One of the great Southron cities, whose famed markets bustle with traders and goods from all across the far lands of Harad and Rhûn.
lotr.waypoint.FERTILE_VALLEY.info.shamii: One of the great Southron cities, whose famed markets bustle with traders and goods from all across the far lands of Harad and Rhûn. Once the stronghold of the Empress Shamiir; now the site of her last resting place.
lotr.waypoint.GARDENS_BERUTHIEL.info: The beautiful hanging gardens of Harad. Said to have been built long ago by a jealous Southron warlord, one among many lovers of the infamous Queen Berúthiel.
lotr.waypoint.AIN_AL_HARAD.info: The Eye of Harad, a fabled city of the South counted as a wonder even among the Haradrim themselves.
lotr.waypoint.GATE_FUINUR.info: Built long ago by the mighty Black Númenórean lord Fuinur, these fortified gates protect the realm of Umbar from foes to the north.
lotr.waypoint.COAST_FORTRESS.info: An ancient Númenórean fortress built to watch over the coastlands. It fell long ago into the hands of the Haradrim.
lotr.waypoint.SANDHILL_TOWN.info: This Southron town which stands upon sandy hills is said to have been the site of a great battle many ages ago.
lotr.waypoint.COAST_RIVER_TOWN.info: A town of the Coast Southrons upon the river Athrassir, which sees many merchant-ships passing between the cedar-woods and the great Southron cities.
lotr.waypoint.COAST_CITY.info: One of the lesser cities of the Southron Coasts, which nonetheless commands many fierce swords and a fearsome devotion to the great Eye of the North.
lotr.waypoint.DESERT_TOWN.info: An encampment of the Southron nomads, where desert-wanderers from many tribes go to trade and tell tales in the shade of the Emyn Lithnen.
lotr.waypoint.SOUTH_DESERT_TOWN.info: Near the edge of the hostile Harad desert stands a surprisingly lively bazaar, where nomad merchants and Far Haradrim poachers trade their exotic goods.
lotr.waypoint.DESERT_RIVER_TOWN.info: A town of the nomads by the source of the Harlanhir, the guiding river on their long road to the Gulf of Harad.
lotr.waypoint.GULF_OF_HARAD.info: Here stands a mighty tower to keep a watch over the sea-passages below, as into the Gulf flow stories, goods, and armies from all across Harad and Rhûn.
lotr.waypoint.GULF_CITY.info: Greatest of the Gulfen cities. It is said that the Southrons of the Gulf sacrifice their old and sick to their lord Mulkhêr, keeping their blood strong.
lotr.waypoint.GULF_FORD.info: The bridge over the great Southern Border-water which separates the Gulf from the lands of Far Harad.
lotr.waypoint.GULF_TRADE_TOWN.info: A trader-town, where exotic goods from East and South are bought and sold. Many Southron traders have made their fortunes here.
lotr.waypoint.GULF_NORTH_TOWN.info: A rich Gulfen city amid the gushing streams of the northern vales, whose people strive to surpass the glory of their southern neighbour.
lotr.waypoint.GULF_EAST_BAY.info: Although said to be a fair land, these eastern shores are notorious as a haunt of corsairs and outlaws from all across Harad and Rhûn.
lotr.waypoint.GULF_EAST_PORT.info: A lesser port town in the far eastern reaches of the Gulfen lands.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_SAND.info: The Sunhorn, a high peak in the northern chain of the Mountains of Harad, and bestowed with much significance by the Haradrim.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_GREEN.info: The Greenhorn, a mighty peak of the Mountains of Harad.
lotr.waypoint.MOUNT_THUNDER.info: The Stormhorn, a mighty peak of the southern Mountains of Harad.
lotr.waypoint.GREAT_PLAINS_NORTH.info: The northernmost regions of the Far Harad grasslands, often visited by poachers from Near Harad who capture and kill exotic beasts for a profit.
lotr.waypoint.GREAT_PLAINS_SOUTH.info: Not far from here are the towering chain of volcanic mountains which the Morwaith fearfully name the Gates of Fire, Narennyn in the Elven-tongue.
lotr.waypoint.GREAT_PLAINS_WEST.info: The Morwaith of the western plains say that beyond the mountains a Great Lion lies watching, awaiting the day when he will swallow all lands and end the world of Men.
lotr.waypoint.GREAT_PLAINS_EAST.info: Among the Morwaith, it is told that here a great ancestral chieftain lies resting, who long ago led their people out from the Shadow into the Sunlands.
lotr.waypoint.GREEN_VALLEY.info: Despite countless battles between the Far Haradrim tribes, these vales at the edge of the forest remain green and lush.
lotr.waypoint.HARAD_LAKES.info: The great inland lakes of Haradwaith, like seas within the plains, home to many flourishing plants and herds of beasts.
lotr.waypoint.LAKE_HARAD.info: The Taurethrim speak of these swamplands, said to be their home in ancient days before a great flooding drove their people southwards.
lotr.waypoint.HARADUIN_MOUTH.info: The mouths of the mighty Haraduin, the longest river in the world.
lotr.waypoint.ISLE_MIST.info: An island, said to be shrouded in mist, that lies at the very southern edge of the world.
lotr.waypoint.TAURELONDE.info: Once a great haven of the Númenóreans stood here, friendly with the old Taurethrim at the height of their power, before the Shadow fell. Long now it has lain empty.
lotr.waypoint.HARAD_HORN.info: The southernmost point of the Haradwaith. Such lands as may lie further south, if any, come not into the lore of the Númenóreans nor the tales of the Southrons.
lotr.waypoint.TOWN_BONES.info: A town built among bones, strange and surreal. The Southrons of the Gulf come here to buy the great Mûmakil from the Morwaith beast-chainers.
lotr.waypoint.HARADUIN_BRIDGE.info: Once the site of a mighty bridge built by the old Taurethrim, long since crumbled away. The new bridge is now traversed only by Morwaith traders and beast-chainers.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_TRADE.info: Near the western edge of the jungles of Harad stands this ancient trader-town, where the old empire grew mighty out of trade with the Númenóreans.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_OLD.info: Though now in ruins, the long-lost seat of the first Taurethrim High Kings inspires awe among travellers and natives alike.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_NORTH.info: A northern outpost of the Taurethrim, fortified against raids from the plains-dwellers.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_EAST.info: An eastern fortress of the Taurethrim built long ago to watch over the lands of the Haraduin.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_CAPITAL.info: The greatest of the old Taurethrim cities that still stands, though its glory is long fallen from the days of the ancient empire.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_DEEP.info: Deep in the jungle stands this lost city, mysterious and forgotten even to many Taurethrim. It is spoken of in their tales as a place of great wonder.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_WATCH.info: A great citadel built in days long past to keep watch over the warmongering tribes of the south.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_CAVES.info: A mysterious city said to be built among caves in the very heart of the earth.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_CITY_STONE.info: A great city of carven stone, once a jewel of the Taurethrim empire, but now a mere shadow of its former greatness.
lotr.waypoint.JUNGLE_LAKES.info: These lakes within the borders of the forests are a place of great natural beauty.
lotr.waypoint.TROLL_ISLAND.info: The Isle of Trolls. It is believed by many that the monstrous race of Half-trolls were first awoken here, though their precise origins remain unknown.
lotr.waypoint.BLACK_COAST.info: The treacherous eastern coasts of Perdorogwaith.
lotr.waypoint.BLOOD_RIVER.info: The Bloodflow, a black and choking stream which runs through the land of the Half-trolls.
lotr.waypoint.SHADOW_POINT.info: The city of the Half-trolls, built on a shore of boiling seas and foundering rocks.
